questions.key_step: Express $ST=\frac y{y'}$, $SN=yy'$ and set the area to $y^3$.
questions.justification: Routine chain: subtangent/subnormal, area formula, algebra to a quadratic in $y'$; options let the student check. Similar demand to 2024-P1-Q1 (L2, DE formed from a limit definition).

questions.key_step: $(xf)'=x^3$ gives $f=\frac{x^3}{4}$; then substitute $u=x^2$ in the integral.
questions.justification: Linear DE with a visible exact derivative, then a standard $\int ue^u$; two routine stages, no insight. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q1 (L2, differentiate integral equation, linear DE).

questions.key_step: Invert to $\frac{dx}{dy}$, recognise Bernoulli in $x$ with $y^2=t$ and $x^{-2}=z$.
questions.justification: Three linked substitutions ($y^2$, inversion to Bernoulli, $x^{-2}$) plus $\int e^t\sin t$; the inversion is less familiar than a plain linear or separable DE, but options allow checking. Above 2026-P2-Q3 (L2, separable with quartic finish), below the L4 non-routine anchors.

questions.key_step: Substitute $t=x^2y^2$ to get $\frac{dt}{dx}=\tan t$.
questions.justification: One familiar substitution matching the left side, then separable and a single initial condition; options available. Same routine class as 2025-P2-Q9 (L2, DE with y(1)=0).

questions.key_step: Linear DE with abstract $f$: integrating factor $\frac{e^{-x}}{f}$.
questions.justification: Standard linear DE; the abstract function adds a little care but no new idea, and the options show the form. Similar to 2024-P1-Q1 (L2).

questions.key_step: L'Hopital in $t$ turns the limit into $3xf-x^2f'=1$, a linear ODE.
questions.justification: Three routine steps (limit as derivative, linear DE, initial value). The L'Hopital-in-$t$ trick is common in coaching sets. (Paper's printed option C and PDF solution had an exponent error; rated on the intended question.)

questions.key_step: Shift to $v=\frac{y^2-3}{x^2-1}$ (centre $(1,3)$ in $X=x^2$, $Y=y^2$), then integrate the rational function.
questions.justification: Long chain: spot $x^2,y^2$ pairing, shift to the intersection point, homogeneous substitution, $\int\frac{v-3}{v^2-4v+5}$ with log and arctan, and heavy back-substitution of a quartic. Options let the final form be matched, but the first step is non-routine; placed with 2026-P2-Q6 (L4, non-routine key idea) and above 2025-P2-Q9 (L2, standard homogeneous DE).

questions.key_step: Normal slope $-\frac1a$ gives tangent slope $a=k$ in $y'=ky$.
questions.justification: Short geometric DE: slope from the normal, separable DE, tangent equation. Routine multi-step with no insight; options present. Like 2024-P1-Q1 (L2).

questions.key_step: Recognise $e^x(g+g')$ with $g=\frac1{\ln x}$.
questions.justification: One familiar pattern applied once; the only care is $\ln x^x=x\ln x$. Same single-move class as 2026-P2-Q4 (L1, king property).

questions.key_step: Differentiate the given identity to get $f(\ln x)$, hence $f(x)$, then $\int e^{e^x}e^x\,dx$.
questions.justification: Three routine stages (differentiate, rename variable to find $f$, substitute); the nested exponential is the only mild trap. Similar to 2021-P2-Q3 (L2, indirect function information).

questions.key_step: Recognise the integrand as $\frac{d}{dx}(x^2e^{\tan x})$ (product rule on $x\cdot xe^{\tan x}$).
questions.justification: One familiar move (product-rule recognition, then differentiate-to-check); no chain. Same single-move level as 2026-P2-Q4 (king property, L1).

questions.key_step: Multiply by $\cos x$ to get $\cos x/\sqrt{1-2\sin^2x}$ and substitute $s=\sin x$.
questions.justification: One standard trick (tan to sin/cos conversion then substitution) applied once; the answer is read off from the standard arcsin form. Comparable to 2024-P2-Q3 (single familiar move, L1).

questions.key_step: Substitute $t=\sin^{-1}(2012^x)$; the derivative factor $\ln2012$ appears in the integrand.
questions.justification: Two small stages (spot the substitution with a constant $\ln a$ factor, then integrate $a^t$) with option bookkeeping of $\log_{2012}e$; routine, no insight. Like 2026-P2-Q3 (routine chain, L2).

questions.key_step: Differentiate $y(x+y)^2=x$ and see that $1+y'$ makes $(x+y)^2+1$ appear, giving $\frac{(x+y)d(x+y)}{(x+y)^2+1}$.
questions.justification: Needs a non-standard link between implicit differentiation and an integral in $x,y$; two ideas linked, with an unfamiliar exact-differential step (options help only by differentiation check). Above routine chains like 2026-P2-Q3 (L2); similar to 2023-P2-Q8 (L3).

questions.key_step: Add $I$ to itself with $x\to-x$ using $\cot^{-1}z+\cot^{-1}(-z)=\pi$ on a symmetric interval.
questions.justification: One well-known property (even weight, $f(x)+f(-x)=\pi$) applied once, then a power integral. Same demand as 2026-P2-Q4 (king property, L1).

questions.key_step: Bound $\cos^8\theta$ between $\frac1{16}$ and $1$ on $(0,\frac\pi4)$.
questions.justification: A single estimate with endpoint values; no computation of the integral. Single-move level like 2024-P2-Q3 (L1).

questions.key_step: Leibniz differentiation of $f$ to show $f>0$, then positivity of $2x^2-\ln x$ via its derivative.
questions.justification: Two ideas linked (sign of integral function via Leibniz, and sign of $2x^2-\ln x$), each routine but needing care that $f(1)$ is not $0$. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q8 (integral function monotonicity, L3).

questions.key_step: Integrate by parts in $t$ to get $\pi\cos x-2\sin x$, then use the amplitude $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.
questions.justification: Routine two-stage chain: parameter integral by parts, then maximum of $a\cos x+b\sin x$; no insight. Like 2023-P2-Q9 (linear DE then maximum, L2).

questions.key_step: $[x-2]=1$ on $[3,4)$, so the curve is the strip $1\le x+3y<2$ of height $\frac13$ over width $1$.
questions.justification: Chain of standard steps: decode greatest-integer equation, sketch the strip, compute a parallelogram area. Close to 2021-P1-Q2 (area of a polygonal region, L2).

questions.key_step: $[\cos t]=-1$ on $(\frac\pi2,\frac{3\pi}2)$, so $f(x)=\frac\pi2-x$ and the region is a right triangle.
questions.justification: Routine multi-step: evaluate integral of a step function on two pieces, graph a line, triangle area. Easier than 2021-P2-Q19 (greatest-integer breakpoints, L4) because there are no breakpoints to locate; level 2 in the same chain-length class as 2026-P2-Q3.

questions.key_step: Differentiate the integral relation in x and eliminate e^y using the relation itself.
questions.justification: Single differentiation of an integral relation with a variable upper limit plus one substitution; no insight needed, like 2023-P2-Q1 (L2, differentiate integral equation). Four closely worded options but the route is routine.

questions.key_step: Factorise the quartic into circle x^2+y^2=4 and lines y=+-1, then identify the intended bounded region.
questions.justification: Spotting the factorisation (quadratic in x^2) and then a circular-strip area with an inverse-sine evaluation; slightly above plain area questions such as 2021-P1-Q2 (L2) and 2025-P2-Q2 (L2) because of the factorisation and the region ambiguity. Recent ratings lean higher.

questions.key_step: Substitute x=4/t on [2,4] so that f(4/t)=f(t).
questions.justification: One familiar substitution, applied once, then add; same weight as the king-property question 2026-P2-Q4 (L1). Slightly easier than a full Advanced item since the integrand is not specified and options are numeric.

questions.key_step: Greatest integer takes only values 0/1, giving a-tan^2 1 = cot^2 1, then trig simplification to cos4 form.
questions.justification: Breakpoint analysis for two greatest-integer integrals (need to see a>tan^2 1 and the order of the breakpoints) followed by a half-angle simplification to match the options; options soften it relative to 2021-P2-Q19 (INT, L4, greatest-integer breakpoints), so L3.

questions.key_step: Spot the integrating factor e^{-x^3} so that the inequality says (e^{-x^3} f)' > 0.
questions.justification: Integrating-factor idea applied to an inequality (less drilled than the equality version) plus an IVT argument to decide the attainable options; comparable to 2021-P2-Q3 (MCQ, L2) in format but the idea is less familiar, so L3. Single chapter, so no multi-concept floor.

questions.key_step: t = tan x reduces it to 1/sqrt(a+(a-b)t^2); choose log or arcsin by the sign of a-b.
questions.justification: One standard substitution and two standard integral forms, with a case split on the sign of a-b; routine chain, no insight, like 2026-P2-Q3 (L2, routine chain). Four options each need the condition checked, which keeps it at 2 rather than 1.

questions.key_step: Area 4a^2=64 gives a=4, then x dy - y dx = x^2 d(y/x) integrates the ODE.
questions.justification: Two short routine chains (area of a parabolic segment, a linear ODE solved by the d(y/x) trick) and four simple checks; no real insight, like 2021-P2-Q5 (MCQ, L2). Two chapters, so the 2.5 multi-correct floor applies to the adjusted level.

questions.key_step: Reconstruct the falling cubic with zeros a,0,c and use c>|a| to see the positive lobe dominates.
questions.justification: Four statements, each needing a careful sign/area judgement with reversed limits; the key is comparing two lobes through c>|a|. Less demanding than 2023-P1-Q3 (MCQ, L4, IVT-style area balancing), since the shape is fixed, so L3. Figure missing in the PDF (reconstructed).

questions.key_step: Integral of an inverse: substitute x=f(t) (or use the rectangle identity) to get pi^2/2 - 2, then bound-check options.
questions.justification: The inverse-function integral trick is familiar but not routine, and four statements each need a numerical-bound check with no calculator; comparable to 2021-P2-Q3 (MCQ, L2) in format but with a less common key step, so L3. Two concepts (inverse functions and integral estimates) also trigger the multi-correct floor of 2.5 but L3 is already above it.

questions.key_step: Differentiate the integral equation to get f = x/(1+x^2), then analyse asymptote, range, extremes and f(|x|)=k.
questions.justification: Recovering f from a two-integral equation is routine (as 2023-P2-Q1, L2), but then four statements about asymptotes, injectivity/surjectivity, tangents and a count of solutions each need a genuine check, like 2026-P1-Q7 (MCQ, L3). Two concepts so the 2.5 floor is satisfied anyway.

questions.key_step: Area of the parabola region inside the ellipse gives $a+b=5$; then sign changes of $2x(x^2-1)(x^2-4)$.
questions.justification: Two-stage: split-area computation with the intersection at x=1 and an exact value to read off a, b (precision risk), then Leibniz and a sign-change check at five points including x=0. Comparable to 2025-P2-Q6 (L4, area under curve with parabola in MCQ) and heavier than 2026-P2-Q8 (L2). Two chapters, so the multi-correct floor does not bind.

questions.key_step: Combine the two radicals over a common root and spot the exact derivative $2\sqrt{(x-a)(b-x)}$.
questions.justification: Single recognition (common denominator gives an exact derivative) followed by routine evaluation, then four option checks; no further idea needed. Similar demand to 2024-P2-Q16 (L2) and a little harder than the one-move 2021-P2-Q11 (L1). Option (D) has no data, so it is a quick elimination.

questions.key_step: The condition means period $6$; one period is a triangle of area $9$.
questions.justification: One familiar move (periodicity, area of one period) followed by four multiplications. Same one-trick demand as 2021-P2-Q17 (L1) and 2026-P2-Q4 (L1).

questions.key_step: Subtract 1 ($Y=y-1$) to separate variables, then read the conic $(y-1)^2=C(x^2-1)$ and test four statements.
questions.justification: Two linked ideas: spotting the shift/solving the DE, then classifying the resulting conic by the sign of C on |x|<1 versus |x|>1 and axis length. The DE is routine (cf. 2021-P2-Q4, L3 MCQ on linear DEs and function families) but the PDF gives no solution and the four conic statements each need a check. Multi-concept MCQ (DE plus conics), so floor 2.5 is satisfied.

questions.key_step: Multiply and divide by $\sqrt{\sec^2x+3}$ to split into $\frac{dt}{\sqrt{4+t^2}}$ and $\frac{\sqrt3\,d\theta}{\sqrt{4-\theta^2}}$.
questions.justification: The decisive step (multiply/divide by the root and split so two different substitutions apply) is outside the usual single-substitution pattern (F1), and four options each need an identity check; no insight beyond that. Near 2025-P2-Q16 (L4, tan^-1 integral needing a non-obvious step) but with option support and standard forms, so one lower; matches the average-Advanced L3 (2021-P1-Q15 style).

questions.key_step: $f'g'=f'g+fg'$ gives $\frac{g'}{g}=\frac{-3}{x-3}$; its sign decides monotonicity.
questions.justification: Routine chain: translate the 'mistake' into an equation, separate variables, read signs; the only subtlety is that g(4)=1 fixes just the branch x>3. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q8 (L2, separable DE with monotonicity) and 2024-P1-Q1 (L2). Multi-concept MCQ (DE and monotonicity) so the adjusted level is lifted to the 2.5 floor.

questions.key_step: Recognise $\sin^{-1}e^x+\cos^{-1}e^x=\frac\pi2$ and the substitution $t=\tan^{-1}e^x$ that leaves $\int\frac{dt}{P+t}$.
questions.justification: Two moderately familiar moves (inverse-trig identity, substitution t=tan^-1 e^x) with a log finish and an improper limit; the integrand looks forbidding but the chain is short. Easier than 2025-P2-Q16 (L4) which needed a king-type idea; sits above 2024-P2-Q16 (L2). The stem is also garbled, which lowers confidence.

questions.key_step: Odd functions integrate to zero on $[-1,1]$ and $[x^2]=0$ there, so only $D\sin|x|$ survives.
questions.justification: One familiar property (odd/even symmetry) plus the observation [x^2]=0; PDF leaves the D part unfinished. It stays at the bottom of the scale, similar to the one-move 2021-P2-Q6 (MCQ, L1) and the king property question 2026-P2-Q4 (L1). Two concepts (symmetry and GIF), so the adjusted level is lifted to the 2.5 floor.

questions.key_step: LMVT (or bounds on the integrand) gives $f(2)=\frac{1}{2+c^4}$ with $c\in(1,2)$.
questions.justification: Single familiar move (bound the integrand on [1,2]) answers all four options; no insight or long computation. Level-1 type like 2021-P2-Q17 (L1) and a notch below 2021-P2-Q3 (MCQ with IVT/Rolle, L2).

questions.key_step: $\ln(x+1)<x$ and $e^x>x+1$ turn the integrands into $\frac1x$ and $\frac1{x+1}$.
questions.justification: Two short comparisons built on two standard inequalities, each applied once; no computation. Slightly above one-move L1 because both integrals and the combined option D must be judged; like 2021-P2-Q3 (L2) and 2024-P2-Q16 (L2).

questions.key_step: Evaluate $I_n$ in closed form (by parts or $t=\sec x+\tan x$), then test four statements.
questions.justification: One non-obvious but well-known device ($t=\sec x+\tan x$ or parts with a perfect-differential partner) gives a closed form; four numeric checks follow, with a near-miss option (7/12 vs 5/12). Comparable to 2026-P2-Q4 (L3, single trick plus execution); less delicate than 2025-P2-Q16 (L4).

questions.key_step: Divide by $x^2$ and substitute $u=x-3/x$ to reduce the quartic denominator to $u^2+u+5$.
questions.justification: One recognised substitution (the $x\mp k/x$ trick on a near-reciprocal quartic) followed by a completed square and four evaluations; the trick is practised but not universal, and the paper gives no hint. Between 2026-P2-Q4 (L3) and 2025-P2-Q16 (L4).

questions.key_step: Recognise $(x y'-y)/x^2=(y/x)'$, integrate, apply $f(1)=1$, then test extremum and values.
questions.justification: Routine linear DE, then a second-derivative test and two evaluations; several standard steps, no insight. Same chain as 2023-P2-Q9 (linear DE then maximum, L2). Two concepts (DE + maxima) in an MCQ, so the 2.5 floor applies.

questions.key_step: Spot $d(x^2+y^2)$ and $d(x/y)$ in the ratio, separate, integrate, and match equivalent forms.
questions.justification: Needs recognising two exact differentials in a disguised ratio (idea availability is moderate) and then matching an equivalent implicit form; option (B) as printed is mis-typed (reconstructed). Comparable to 2023-P2-Q1 (L2) plus a non-obvious grouping step.

questions.key_step: Interpret $\min$ and $\max$ level curves as a hash plus a square, giving four unit squares.
questions.justification: Needs a clear picture of unfamiliar min/max level curves, but the computation is trivial and the statements are 'less than or equal' tests; routine-plus-picture. Easier than 2021-P1-Q2 (L3, region from four lines).

questions.key_step: Group terms into $d(xy)$ and $d(x^3y^{3/2})$ (or test exactness).
questions.justification: Standard exact-equation work with fractional powers; routine with options to compare. Stem is mis-printed (factor $y$ missing) and reconstructed from the PDF working. Level 2 like 2026-P2-Q3 (separable DE with an awkward finish, L2).

questions.key_step: Set $x=0$ for $f(0)$, differentiate the integral equation with the Leibniz rule.
questions.justification: Two routine moves (initial value, Leibniz) chained, options to match; no real insight. Similar chain to 2023-P2-Q1 (integral equation to DE, L2).

questions.key_step: Get $f(0)=2$, then $f'(0)$ and $f''(0)$ from the derived DE.
questions.justification: Short follow-up using the previous part; evaluating derivatives at $0$ needs care but is routine. Level 2 as for 2023-P2-Q1 (L2).

questions.key_step: Solve the linear DE with integrating factor $e^x$ and standard exponential-trig integrals; fix constant by $f(0)=2$.
questions.justification: Longest part of the paragraph: integrating factor, two exponential-trig integrals and constant fixing, with a trap option; execution-heavy but options allow elimination. A notch above 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).

questions.key_step: Differentiate both relations, solve for $f$ and $g$ via product and ratio.
questions.justification: Two differentiations and a small algebraic solve; routine chain with no insight. Level 2 as 2023-P2-Q1 (integral equation to a function, L2).

questions.key_step: Differentiate the two integral relations to get $fg$ and $g/f$, hence $f=x^2+1$, $g=x^3+x$.
questions.justification: Two differentiations, a division to solve for $f^2$, then a routine polynomial integration; no insight needed and options allow checking. Same routine-chain demand as 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).

questions.key_step: Spot $\frac{d}{dx}\frac{\phi}{y}=\frac{\phi'y-\phi y'}{y^2}$ so the equation reads $(\phi/y)'=1$.
questions.justification: One familiar quotient-rule recognition, then a two-line integration with the initial data. Comparable to 2024-P1-Q1 (L2, derive a linear DE, solve with a condition).

questions.key_step: Factor $x$ out of the root and use $t=1-\frac1x$ with $dt=\frac{dx}{x^2}$.
questions.justification: Needs the previous part's result and a non-obvious substitution ($t=1/x$ type, hidden by the $\frac1{x^2}$) before a standard integral; options let the student check. Between 2026-P2-Q4 (L1, king property) and 2025-P2-Q16 (L4); the same paragraph-based demand as 2021-P2-Q16 (Para SCQ, L3).

questions.key_step: Substitute $g=x-1$ and check four statements (monotonicity, area, extrema, differentiability of $|g|$).
questions.justification: Four short statements, each a routine check on a line or on $|x-1|$, once the paragraph result is known; no real idea but several verifications. Similar to 2021-P1-Q2 (L2, area of simple linear region).

questions.key_step: Translate the geometric area condition into $|y'|=\frac{xy}{2}$, fix the sign with $f(3)$, then bound an area with a non-elementary integral.
questions.justification: Long chain: geometry to ODE (sub-tangent, absolute value), solve and fix the sign using both data points, find the intersection with the line, set up the area and estimate $\int e^{(x^2-1)/4}$ without a closed form. Heavier than 2023-P2-Q1 (L2); comparable stages and precision risk to 2025-P2-Q6 (L4, area from a geometric condition).

questions.key_step: Evaluate $\int_0^x\cos(t-x)dt=\sin x$ before differentiating; then $f'=(f-1)\cos x$ and find the range.
questions.justification: Integral equation with $x$ inside the integrand, then a linear ODE and a range-and-count step; three linked ideas but all standard. Same shape as 2023-P2-Q1 (L2, differentiate an integral equation) plus the extra range stage, so one level above.

questions.key_step: Treat $\int_0^1f$ as constant $k$; get $f=kx^2+1$, $k=\frac32$; shortest distance parabola-line at slope $1$.
questions.justification: Three stages (constant trick, Leibniz and self-consistency, shortest distance) all standard; numerical format with no options but low precision risk. Comparable to 2024-P2-Q13 (INT, L3, integral-defined functions) and 2023-P2-Q8 (L3).

questions.key_step: Region is a triangle with base $3$ and height $\frac{6}{2a+1}$; solve $\frac{9}{2a+1}=3$.
questions.justification: Routine: intersect two lines, area of a triangle, solve one equation. Same demand as 2021-P1-Q2 (L2, area of a linear region); no insight and little precision risk.

questions.key_step: Reduce $yy''=2y'^2$ to $y'=ky^2$, solve with two conditions, then split the area at the crossing point.
questions.justification: Reduction of order (familiar), two-point initial conditions, and an area with a switch of the lower curve and an unusual boundary description ('line $f(x)=2/e$'); numerical answer with no options. Comparable to 2025-P2-Q9 (Numerical, L2, DE then evaluate) but with an extra area stage, so one level higher.

questions.key_step: Combine the terms to $\frac{x^2+1}{x^4+1}$, divide by $x^2$ and use $t=x-\frac1x$.
questions.justification: A separable DE, then the well-known $x-\frac1x$ substitution applied to a rational function with a limit at $-\infty$, and a final least-$(p+q)$ reading. Standard coaching trick (idea available) but chained; below 2025-P2-Q16 (L4, king-type substitution) and above 2026-P2-Q4 (L1).

questions.key_step: One-line identity: integral of f^n f' is end values only; sign choice f(1)=-f(0) forced by 54.
questions.justification: Same family of definite-integral identity questions as 2024-P2-Q16 (L3) but with only a familiar substitution and short chain; a notch easier than 2023-P2-Q1 (L3, DE from integral equation).

questions.key_step: |x+2|+|x-5|>=7 gives r=7, then quadratic-in-y discriminant gives a semicircle-type area.
questions.justification: Three linked stages (modulus plateau, conic as two branches, semicircle area); comparable to 2021-P1-Q2 (L3) area-by-regions, lighter than 2025-P2-Q6 (L4).

questions.key_step: Area of y=|f(|x|)| gives k=4; circumcentre on x=1 and the diameter gives height 4.
questions.justification: Two chapters in a numerical question with four short stages (graph transformations, area, perpendicular bisector, rectangle); similar chaining to 2023-P1-Q7 (L3) parabola/area with integer data; no hidden idea so not 4.

questions.key_step: |x| even kills odd powers; remaining terms telescope as 1/(k(k+1)).
questions.justification: Parity plus termwise integration plus telescoping limit, numerical answer; like 2025-P1-Q11 (L4) in being a series-integral combination but with every move familiar, so one level lower; near 2024-P2-Q16 (L3).

questions.key_step: Binomial ratio = prod (3n-r)/(2n-r), then Riemann sum of ln((3-x)/(2-x)).
questions.justification: Limit-as-sum of a factorial ratio is a standard but multi-step trick: recognise the product, convert to integral, integrate two logs; no options to check. Near 2026-P1-Q12 (L4, telescoping product) but with a more familiar idea.

questions.key_step: Newton's cooling: separable DE with two conditions.
questions.justification: Routine separable DE with a word-problem set-up and two substitutions, like 2026-P2-Q3 (L2) and 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

questions.key_step: Tangent length sqrt(S1) from Q(0,3), then e^{6r}=2.
questions.justification: Two short routine pieces from different chapters, no insight; like 2026-P2-Q2 (L2) perpendicular tangents in being a few standard steps.

questions.key_step: (f^{-1})'(0)=1/f'(2) with f(2)=0 and Leibniz derivative.
questions.justification: One familiar chain (Leibniz then inverse-derivative formula); more routine steps than a level-1 single move; below 2023-P2-Q8 (L4). Note the printed key/branch ambiguity.

questions.key_step: Symmetry in both axes, then 4*integral of (1 - x^{2/5}).
questions.justification: Area with a fractional power curve: symmetry plus a single power-rule integral; slightly more than one move because of the cusp/symmetry reading; below 2025-P2-Q2 (L3).

questions.key_step: Strip [k,k+1): area k+2/3, then sum an arithmetic series.
questions.justification: Greatest-integer/fractional-part area is a routine chain once the strip pattern is seen; easier than 2021-P2-Q19 (L4, locating breakpoints of [sqrt(10x/(x+1))]).

questions.key_step: Eliminate y, cancel the 2t terms, then 0/0 limit of an integral (L'Hopital/FTC).
questions.justification: Chain of three routine steps with no non-routine idea (only the cancellation of 2t is a trap). Similar to 2023-P2-Q1 (L2, integral relation plus routine calculus). Numerical format keeps it at 2, not 1.

questions.key_step: Shift u=x-r makes the 11 integrals identical; then |cubic| split at roots.
questions.justification: Routine chain: shift, symmetry, split at roots, polynomial integrals. Precision risk small. Below 2021-P2-Q19 (L4, greatest-integer breakpoints) and comparable to 2024-P2-Q16 (L3) only in length, not insight; no hidden idea.

questions.key_step: Recognise the exact differential d(x sin(x^2 y)) and solve x sin(x^2y)+y=0.
questions.justification: Exact-equation test plus finding the potential with a composite argument x^2y is less routine than a linear/separable DE (2023-P2-Q1, L2; 2026-P2-Q3, L2); the final value needs the insight that no explicit alpha is needed. Numerical answer, no options.

questions.key_step: Rewrite sin4x via tan, substitute t=tan^2x, recognise e^t(f+f').
questions.justification: Needs a non-obvious rewrite of sin4x in tan x and recognition of the e^t(f+f') pattern for a rational f; a strong student knows the pattern but the chain is 3-4 stages. Comparable to 2025-P1-Q11 (L4, series expansion) but with a given answer form that allows checking, hence 3.

questions.key_step: sin x = 2 sin(x/2)cos(x/2) gives the meeting point; set one part's area equal to 1 and reject k=2+sqrt2.
questions.justification: Standard area-bisection with an inverse-trig limit, algebra with half-angle identities and a root rejection; numerical answer so slips are costly. Nearer to 2021-P1-Q2 (L2) in demand, but more algebra and a domain trap, so 3.

questions.key_step: t = tan(theta) converts the integrand to sin^4 cos^6; apply Wallis.
questions.justification: One standard substitution followed by Wallis' formula: a routine two-step chain with no insight. Easier than 2025-P2-Q16 (L4); similar in spirit to 2026-P2-Q4 (L1) but with longer evaluation.

questions.key_step: Integration by parts on each linear piece (or test f=1 to get 0 at once).
questions.justification: Parts on two linear pieces and collecting coefficients, or the f=1 test; no heavy computation. Less demanding than 2024-P2-Q13 (L3, piecewise f with g=integral); routine chain so 2.

questions.key_step: x=tan t, by parts, then king property on ln(1+tan t).
questions.justification: Well-known three-stage chain (substitution, by parts, king); each stage standard. Easier than 2025-P2-Q16 (L4, king-type with tan^-1 and a quadratic) and harder than 2026-P2-Q4 (L1, single king).

questions.key_step: 1/e^2+1/e'^2=1 gives f(e)=e/sqrt(e^2-1) and f(f(e))=e; then two elementary integrals.
questions.justification: Two short stages across two chapters (conic relation, then integration); the involution f(f(e))=e saves work but is not hidden. Routine chain so 2, with the two-chapter nature as a minor tie-breaker.

questions.key_step: Period 2pi plus king property to kill sin(cos x), then sin x = t to reach I2.
questions.justification: Several property applications chained (periodicity, f(2pi-x)=f(x), king, half-range, substitution) with a cancellation insight; numerical with no options. More stages than 2026-P2-Q4 (L1); less delicate than 2025-P2-Q16 (L4).

questions.key_step: Completing the square; zero integral of a square forces $f=x/2$
questions.justification: Needs the unprompted completing-the-square idea and the 'zero integral of a square' argument, then a trivial finish; numerical so no options. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q4 (king property, short idea-led integral) but with a less automatic trick, so a level above it.

questions.key_step: Recurrence $2I_{n+1}=I_n$ from by parts, giving $I_n=\pi/2^{n+1}$
questions.justification: A well-known reduction but the by-parts with the sin(n+1)x factor and the cancellation must be seen; no options. One chain of three standard steps with a precision trap; sits with other integral-recurrence style numericals.

questions.key_step: $f$ is an involution, so $2017$ (odd) compositions equal $f$
questions.justification: One recognition (f is its own inverse, odd number of compositions) then a routine integral and a floor; chain of three routine steps, no insight beyond the involution. Numerical but short.

questions.key_step: Boundary is $\sin x=\sin(y\pm\pi/3)$: straight lines, then area is square minus corner triangles
questions.justification: Needs the unprompted discriminant/identity step to turn a trig inequality into straight lines, plus careful handling of the fold at $y=\pi/6$ and area of a pentagon; numerical, easy to slip. Similar demand to 2023-P1-Q9 (area of piecewise region, L4) and 2021-P1-Q2 (polygon region, L3), one step less routine.

questions.key_step: Area between tangent and curve = trapezium under the tangent minus given area
questions.justification: Read the figure, get the two parallel lines, and subtract a trapezium area from the given area; three routine steps, a single idea. Figure is described in the stem.

questions.key_step: $x\to-x$ gives the complementary fraction, so the integral is half of the integral of the numerator
questions.justification: Standard king-property pairing with a disguised $g^x$ denominator and an even integrand; one familiar move plus a short evaluation. Same demand as 2026-P2-Q4 (king property, L1) with an extra step to recognise the reciprocal, so L2.

questions.key_step: Substitute $\cos y+\sin y$ to get a linear ODE; integrating factor $e^{-e^{-x}}$
questions.justification: Spot the substitution $\cos y+\sin y$ and solve a linear ODE with a double-exponential integrating factor; but the printed question is internally inconsistent, so the rating is on the intended route.

questions.key_step: $P^2+Q^2=\frac{e^{6x}}{a^2+b^2}$ since $(a\cos+b\sin)^2+(a\sin-b\cos)^2=a^2+b^2$
questions.justification: Known integral formulas then a Pythagorean-type simplification; routine chain, large numbers hide the pattern but nothing deep. Level 2 like other routine integral chains.

questions.key_step: $\frac{dV}{dt}=kV^2$ gives $\frac1{V_0}-\frac1V=kt$
questions.justification: A single standard separable rate equation applied twice with substitution; one familiar move, no ambiguity. JEE-Main-level DE.

questions.key_step: Rebuild $f$ piecewise from the two functional relations, then integrate
questions.justification: Translating two functional relations into four pieces and noticing positivity, then four routine integrals; careful bookkeeping but no new idea. Routine chain, L2.

questions.key_step: Solve $f'=f^2$ for $f$, then $\frac{x^2+1}{x^4+1}$ via $x-\frac1x=t$
questions.justification: Two linked ideas: separable DE giving $f=-1/(x+1)$ and the $x-\frac1x$ substitution for $\frac{x^2+1}{x^4+1}$; the second trick is well known but must be recognised unprompted; numerical. Reconstruction of the coefficient noted.

questions.key_step: Spot that $2e^{g^2}$ makes the left side $\frac{d}{dx}(e^{g^2}y^2)$ (or put $w=1-y^2$), then use $g(e)=g(0)$.
questions.justification: Needs two linked ideas: y^2 as the unknown and an integrating factor built from an abstract g; there are no options to check. Each step is routine once seen, so below L4 but above the routine linear/separable DE anchors (L2).

questions.key_step: Solve the separable DE to $f=Ae^{x}(\ln x)^{2n}$ and see that $n\to\infty$ kills $f$ exactly on $(1/e,e)$.
questions.justification: Standard separable DE (L2 level) followed by a limit-of-powers case analysis and the trick that endpoint values do not matter; the infinite values outside the interval are a distraction. Numerical, no options.

questions.key_step: Translate the tangent condition into $g'=Cg$, get $k=12$ from the area, then use the three-tangent triangle formula with $\cot\theta=t$.
questions.justification: Three-stage chain across three chapters (tangent condition to DE, area, parabola tangents) with the value k carried from one part to the next; no options to check. Each stage is moderate, but a slip anywhere ruins the answer. Question-stem style, sits with the L4 stem anchors.

questions.key_step: Spot $x+y=(x+2)+(y-2)$, shift the origin, then solve the homogeneous equation with $Y=vX$.
questions.justification: Routine chain: expand, shift origin, homogeneous substitution, one partial-fraction integral; no insight beyond standard DE technique. Same demand as the homogeneous-type DE anchor.

questions.key_step: Differentiate $\int_0^xf=\lambda f^{n+1}$ to get a separable DE, integrate with $f(0)=0$ and use $f(1)=1$.
questions.justification: Integral equation to separable DE, three routine steps with a symbolic n; the wording is the only difficulty. Same demand as the integral-equation anchor (L2).

questions.key_step: Use $1\le\sin x+\cos x\le\sqrt2$ and monotonicity of $x^s$ in $s$ on $(0,1]$ to sandwich the integrand between $x$ and $x^{\sqrt2}$.
questions.justification: One standard bounding idea (monotone in the exponent) plus a numerical comparison; no hidden difficulty and the answer is a proof. Easier than the L3 integral-inequality anchors, which need an extra observation.

questions.key_step: Apply the Leibniz rule to $g(x)=\int_x^{2x}\frac{f(t)}{t}dt$ and use $f(2x)=f(x)$.
questions.justification: A single familiar move (Leibniz differentiation) followed by substituting the given functional relation; a proof-type question with no computation. JEE-Main level.

questions.key_step: Use $f'(x)=(x-3)(x-4)$ to locate the minimum at $x=4$, then compare $f(3)$, $f(4)$, $f(6)$.
questions.justification: Three routine steps: FTC derivative, sign analysis, evaluation of two integrals; no real insight. Slightly longer than a single-move L1 question and easier than the L3 piecewise g=integral anchor.
